criteria.text: Acute intermittent treatment of hypomobility/off episodes in Parkinson’s disease (approval criterion 2 and FDA indications).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a neurologist (approval criterion 3).
Prescribed concurrently with an anti-Parkinson agent, e.g. levodopa/carbidopa, dopamine agonists (ropinirole), COMT inhibitors (tolcapone), or MAO-B inhibitors (rasagiline) (approval criterion 4).
Hypomobility at the end of the dosing interval or unpredictable on/off episodes (approval criterion 5).
Patient is NOT concurrently taking a 5-HT3 antagonist (e.g. ondansetron, granisetron, dolasetron) (denial criterion 2).

notes: Partial encoding from AK Apokyn/Kynmobi (apomorphine) Criteria Version 1. Original: 10/07/20; Approval: 11/20/20. PDF Effective is printed as 1/11//20 (malformed; commonly rendered 1/11/20). effective_date uses the unambiguous approval date 2020-11-20 rather than the archived stub date 2026-03-01; the source extraction is retained unchanged.

Apokyn injectable is indicated for acute intermittent hypomobility/off episodes associated with advanced Parkinson’s disease; Kynmobi sublingual films are indicated for acute intermittent off episodes in Parkinson’s disease. Approval criteria 1–5 and the concurrent 5-HT3 antagonist denial are encoded. Failure to meet approval criteria is also a denial.
Duration (notes only): Initial Approval up to 3 months; Reauthorization Approval up to 12 months.

Quantity limits (notes only): Apokyn — 5 injections per day / 150 injections per month; Kynmobi — 5 films per day / 150 films per month. Duration and quantity enforcement require manual review; this pack remains partial.

Cautions (notes only): Concomitant antihypertensive medications and vasodilators may increase risk of hypotension, myocardial infarction, falls and injuries. Syncope and hypotension/orthostatic hypotension may occur; monitor blood pressure.

Cautions (notes only): Withdrawal-emergent hyperpyrexia and confusion may occur with rapid dose reduction or withdrawal. May prolong QTc and cause torsades de pointes or sudden death; consider risk factors prior to initiation. Dopamine antagonists may diminish apomorphine effectiveness. Patients 65 years and older were more likely to experience certain adverse events in clinical trials.
